query: In `release/unix/make_scripts_portable.py`, explain what `main` does with each entry of the interpreter's scripts directory so the scripts keep working when the Python distribution is moved: which entries it considers at all; which files it rewrites with a new header and exactly how (including what happens to blank lines at the top of a file); which files it rewrites but keeps the original first line for (a first line that points at another interpreter); and which entries it leaves untouched on disk (non-files, binaries, and anything that produces no content).

operations.name: Selection: only regular files are considered; other directory entries are skipped (left untouched)
operations.needed_for: which entries it considers at all; non-files are left untouched

operations.name: Modification: leading blank lines are ignored, so they are not written back to a rewritten file
operations.needed_for: what happens to blank lines at the top of a file

operations.name: Left untouched: a file whose first non-blank line is not a comment is treated as a binary and yields no content
operations.needed_for: which entries it leaves untouched on disk (binaries)

operations.name: Modification: a header naming this interpreter is replaced by the portable shebang
expressions: data.write(portable_shebang if executable == interpreter else line)
operations.needed_for: which files it modifies and how

operations.name: Left untouched: a file that produced no content is not written back
operations.needed_for: which entries it leaves untouched on disk (no content)

dependencies.name: Only first lines naming a path under the interpreter's own directory are examined; any other first line is copied through unchanged and the file is still rewritten
dependencies.needed_for: which files it rewrites but keeps the original first line for

dependencies.name: The executable named in the header is resolved and compared with this interpreter before the header is replaced
The rest of the file after the header is appended unchanged, and the result is collected before the emptiness check
dependencies.needed_for: what happens to the rest of a modified file

revisions.reviewer_note: clarify file selection and modification versus preservation
revisions.change: Question now asks separately which entries are considered, which files are modified (and how) and which are preserved or not written back. Operation names and a needed_for mapping state the same three roles. Expressions unchanged. On re-reading the code the question was made exact: a file whose first line points at another interpreter is rewritten (header copied through, leading blank lines dropped), not left untouched; only non-files, binaries and no-content files are left untouched on disk.
